title: Update on GPFirst Programme at Changi General Hospital
what_it_is: Update on GPFirst Programme at Changi General Hospital

sections.label: GPFirst emergency care referrals
sections.summary: GPFirst refers patients needing emergency care to the ED with priority and a $50 subsidy, and has expanded to more hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Patients assessed by the participating GPs as requiring emergency care would be referred on and be given priority to be seen earlier at the ED.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These patients will be given a $50 subsidy on their ED bill to help offset the cost of their GP visit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 2014 to 2017, there was a reduction of about 8.5% in the self-referred attendances at CGH ED, which may be attributed to GPFirst and other measures implemented during this period of time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH has expanded GPFirst beyond CGH's region in phases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As of September 2020, GPFirst has been expanded to involve more GPs around Khoo Teck Puat Hospital and the Urgent Care Centre @Admiralty Medical Centre, and will be progressively implemented in the region surrounding Sengkang General Hospital, National University Hospital and Ng Teng Fong General Hospital by the end of 2021.
